A.notes: A has a strong editorial-field-report concept carried through the whole page: plate labels, restrained illustration, the stamped data section, and bilingual hierarchy all feel like one system. The scroll strip shows the 140-hectare grid progressing meaningfully, which is the clearest story-led motion of the two, though some small text and the very tall pinned section feel a bit sparse in static views.

B.notes: B is clean and coherent, with a clear mangrove-root/sprout motif and solid bilingual presentation, but it reads more like a polished standard non-profit landing page than a distinctive public-interest identity. In the scroll frames, motion appears minimal or mostly equivalent to normal scrolling, so I can't credit it as telling the story beyond basic section transitions.

raw.why: A turns the brief into a more distinctive, better-integrated visual system and uses scroll progression more meaningfully to communicate the 140-hectare figure.
